verses.text: "The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed to pay them one silver coin for the day, and he sent them into his vineyard.
"About nine o'clock in the morning he went out again. He saw others standing in the market place doing nothing.
He told them, 'You also go and work in my vineyard, and I will pay you whatever is fair.' So they went.
"He went out again about twelve o'clock and about three o'clock in the afternoon and did the same thing.
About five o'clock in the afternoon he went out and found still others standing around. He asked them, 'Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?'
"'Because no one has hired us,' they answered. "He said to them, 'You also go and work in my vineyard, and you will get whatever is fair.'
"When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, 'Call the workers and pay them their wages. Begin with the last ones hired and go on to the first.'
"The workers who were hired about five o'clock came, and each of them received one silver coin.
So when the first workers came, they expected to receive more. But each of them also received one silver coin.
When they received it, they began to complain about the landowner.
They said, 'These men who were hired last worked only one hour. But you have paid them the same as us, and we have done most of the work in the heat of the day.'
"But he answered one of them, 'Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree to work for one silver coin?
Take your pay and go. I want to give the man who was hired last the same as I gave you.
Do I not have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you jealous because I am generous?'
"So the last will be first, and the first will be last. Many are invited, but few are chosen."
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve followers aside on the way and talked to them.
"We are going up to Jerusalem," he said. "The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the teachers of the law. They will sentence him to death.
Then they will hand him over to people who are not Jews. They will make fun of him, whip him and nail him to a cross. But on the third day he will be raised to life."
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt down and asked him for a favour.
"What do you want?" Jesus asked. She said, "Promise that one of my two sons may sit at your right side and the other at your left side in your kingdom."
Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup of suffering that I am going to drink, and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with?" "We can," they answered.

Jesus said to them, "You will certainly drink from my cup, and be baptised with the baptism I am baptised with. But it is not for me to say who will sit at my right side or my left side. These places belong to those my Father has prepared them for."
When the other ten followers heard about this, they were angry with the two brothers.
Jesus called them together and said, "You know that the rulers of the nations like to show their power over their people. Their important leaders order them around.
It must not be like that with you. Instead, anyone who wants to be important among you must be your servant.
And anyone who wants to be first must be your slave.
In the same way, the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve others, and to give his life to set many people free."
As Jesus and his followers were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
Two blind men were sitting by the side of the road. When they heard that Jesus was going by, they shouted, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
The crowd told them off and told them to be quiet. But they shouted even louder, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
Jesus stopped and called them. "What do you want me to do for you?" he asked.
"Lord," they answered, "we want to be able to see."
Jesus felt sorry for them and touched their eyes. Straight away they could see, and they followed him.
